column5: The relationship between supernovae and neutron stars is that neutron stars are formed as remnants after a supernova explosion. Specifically, when a massive star undergoes a supernova explosion, its core collapses under its own gravity if it is sufficiently massive. This collapse can result in the formation of a neutron star, which has a radius on the order of 10 kilometers and a mass of about 1.4 times the mass of the Sun. Therefore, supernovae are the explosive events that lead to the creation of neutron stars.
